messages:
Alex (design): Quick note — I prototyped a clustered sidepane alternative that groups by task rather than surface (eg. 'Deploy & Traffic', 'Models & Versions', 'Observability'). Sketch: https://figma.com/file/xxxx/sidepane-clusters. Thoughts?
Maria (frontend): Really interesting. Does the clustering keep the global routes shallow? worried about deep links like /models/123/rollouts
Sam (product): Our customers want stable, bookmarkable URLs for audits and support. Can we guarantee each cluster item maps to a unique URL? e.g., /console/models -> /console/models/:id?rollout
Alex (design): Yes — each cluster entry would be a router root. Proposal: clicking a cluster header toggles the group; opening an item navigates to a canonical route. Keyboard focus should land on the first item in the opened group.
Jess (eng-runtime): Implementation note: prefer explicit routes rather than hash fragments so server-side redirects and SSO deep links work. Keep routes like /console/{cluster}/{resource}/{id}
Elena (a11y-bot): a11y nit: if headers are collapsible, add aria-expanded on the button and use role="tree"/"treeitem"? Also ensure focus is trapped only when a modal opens, not for nav expansion.
Maria (frontend): Agree on aria-expanded. Also we need to preserve back-button behavior: expanding a cluster shouldn't push history, but navigating to an item should. Otherwise users get a noisy history stack.
Sam (product): Small copy tweak: in clusters where items are cross-functional, use labels like 'Observability (metrics & traces)' instead of nested words. Helps scannability for new users.
Alex (design): New breadcrumb behaviour: breadcrumbs should show cluster > subsection > page, and each crumb is a link. If the user arrived via a deep link, the breadcrumb should still reflect the logical cluster, not necessarily the navigation history.
Jess (eng-runtime): Edge case — pinned routes (customer pinned dashboards) should bypass collapsing logic and always appear at top. We can add a pinned boolean on nav items in the manifest.
Maria (frontend): Question about deep linking to modals (eg. share invite modal). Do we want URL fragments for transient UI or real paths? Fragments are easier but not shareable with server-side introspection.
Sam (product): Preference: persistent state -> full URL; transient overlays -> query param like ?modal=invite. This allows shareable links but keeps ephemeral state separate.
Elena (a11y-bot): Also ensure focus is correctly restored after navigating back from a modal. Use element focus management and visible focus rings.
Alex (design): UX checklist I propose before rollout: 1) canonical routes mapped 1:1 2) keyboard nav through clusters 3) ARIA attributes for collapsible headers 4) breadcrumb reflect cluster context 5) deep link test cases (SSO, bookmarked URLs)
Jess (eng-runtime): I'll add a small router manifest sample to the infra repo. Snippet for discussion:

  routes:
    - path: /console/deploy
      cluster: deploy-traffic
    - path: /console/models/:id
      cluster: model-management

Maria (frontend): I'll experiment with CSS transitions for expand/collapse to avoid content jump. Keep reduced-motion preference in mind.
Sam (product): Can we get a quick user test with 6 customers on Monday? Validate findability of models vs routing expectations.
Alex (design): I'll schedule a 20m async test and share prototype. Thanks all — leaving this open for final signoff. :thumbsup:
